answer: A Code contribution passing automated tests backed by a refundable deposit makes identity cost real work: the code contribution is reviewed line by line, the refundable deposit is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so a Sybil farm must produce genuine, reviewed output for every fake account it wants. A cipher that appears twice is the tell: the same work cannot earn two identities. When the opal settles over the beacon, the work holds because every task carried its own review.
